papers.title: Discovery of frameshift-associated TCRs following personalized neoantigen vaccination in a patient with osteosarcoma
papers.abstract: Personalized antigen-directed immunotherapies, including personalized cancer vaccines, are emerging as promising therapeutic modalities for a range of cancer types. Immune monitoring can be used to evaluate the efficacy of a vaccine in stimulating the immune response pre- and post-vaccination; however, such approaches typically stop short of identifying which T cell receptors (TCRs) are functionally driving therapeutic responses. Here, we present a case report of immune monitoring and subsequent TCR discovery experiments following administration of personalized cancer vaccines in a patient with locally recurrent osteosarcoma. Whole PBMCs were stimulated with vaccine peptides (>16 AA) in vitro for 11 days, after which IFN{gamma} ELISPOT identified total T cell responses for 12 of 15 tested peptides post-vaccination. In vitro expanded samples were submitted for 10x single-cell TCR sequencing, from which 26 TCRs were chosen for generation of TCR-T cells based on clonal expansion and culture specificity. Of the generated TCR-T cells, 25 produced functional TCRs, 4 of which were specific to vaccine peptides. However, downstream testing revealed each was MHC class-II restricted. To address this, we repeated the in vitro stimulations with co-cultures of isolated CD8+ T cells with autologous dendritic cells, and cultures of whole PBMCs with anti-MHC class-II blocking antibody. These cultures yielded 10 additional TCRs, 2 of which were responsive to a vaccine peptide containing a MAP2 frameshift mutation. These findings demonstrate an effective approach for leveraging post-vaccination expanded antigen-specific T cell populations for discovery of novel T cell receptors for downstream cellular therapies.

papers.title: Rationally Engineered Self-Assembling Protein Nanoparticles for Allergen-Specific Peanut Allergy Immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Peanut allergy is a prevalent immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated food allergy that can cause life-threatening anaphylaxis. Current treatment options provide limited efficacy and variable durability of protection. While allergen-displaying virus-like particles (VLPs) have shown promise, their development is often constrained by limited design flexibility and manufacturing complexity. Here, we develop self-assembling protein nanoparticles (SApNPs) displaying the major allergens Ara h 2 and Ara h 6 as a modular platform for peanut allergy immunotherapy. Using the 60-mer TIP60 scaffold, we engineer nanoparticles by expanding particle size through -helical insertion and replacing the human myosin-X segment with evolutionarily distant catfish homologs, followed by structure-guided and evolution-inspired optimization to enhance thermostability while minimizing human sequence content. Formulated with a Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, these allergen-displaying SApNPs confer robust protection against peanut-induced anaphylaxis in both prophylactic and therapeutic settings. Mechanistically, SApNPs exhibit prolonged lymph node retention, sustained presentation on follicular dendritic cells, and enhanced germinal center responses compared with soluble allergens, promoting allergen-specific IgG and functional T cell responses while limiting IgE escalation. Collectively, these findings establish allergen-displaying SApNPs as a rationally engineered, scalable, and modular platform for peanut allergy treatment with potential applicability to other allergic diseases.

papers.title: Xenoglycosylation of the HIV-1 Glycan Shield Promotes Cross-Clade Neutralization and Diverse Human Antibody Lineages
papers.abstract: Despite advances in HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env)-based vaccine design, eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) remains a central challenge. Here, we identify core (1,3)-fucose as a key modulator of neutralizing antibody (NAb) induction and breadth. Uncleaved prefusion-optimized (UFO) trimers and self-assembling protein nanoparticles (SApNPs) produced in High Five (Hi5) insect cells incorporate core (1,3)-fucose into the Env glycan shield. Crystal structures of Hi5-produced BG505 UFO trimers in complex with bNAbs confirm native-like Env architecture and epitope presentation. In wild-type mice, these trimers and SApNPs elicit robust autologous and heterologous NAb responses. We then engineer Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells to co-express three insect- and plant-derived core (1,3)-fucosyltransferases. The resulting immunogens carry fucosylated mammalian glycans and elicit cross-clade NAb responses in mice, supporting an important role for core (1,3)-fucose in broadened neutralization. Env-specific IgE responses suggest engagement of associated immune pathways during vaccination. In ATX-Gx humanized mice, core (1,3)-fucosylated, glycan-trimmed Env elicits detectable cross-clade neutralization by week 11. Single-cell analysis identifies distinct human antibody lineages with cross-clade activity and noncanonical Env recognition. Repertoire and functional analyses uncover putatively related lineage members across two animals within the same group. Together, these findings support xenoglycosylation as a promising, germline-agnostic strategy for HIV-1 vaccine design.

papers.title: Cholesterol constrains pore formation by mammalian gasdermins
papers.abstract: Pyroptosis is a lytic form of cell death executed by gasdermin pores. Through a CRISPR screen to uncover macrophage genes required for gasdermin D (GSDMD) pore activity, we identify the endosome adaptor Rabgef1 as a positive regulator of pore formation. Rabgef1 deficiency preserves NT-GSDMD membrane binding but prevents NT-GSDMD oligomerization and lytic death. Mechanistic analyses revealed that Rabgef1 deficiency is associated with an overabundance of cholesterol in the plasma membrane. Cholesterol depletion or redistribution through multiple approaches restores GSDMD oligomerization and pyroptosis. The Rabgef1-mediated control of membrane cholesterol and pore formation was found to be a general regulator of the gasdermin family. In cancer cells, organoids, and tumors, cholesterol reduction sensitizes resistant cells to GSDME pyroptosis driven by synthetic mRNAs, chemogenetic induction, and chemotherapy treatment. These results establish membrane cholesterol content as an endogenous checkpoint for gasdermin-mediated pyroptotic cell death during the execution phase, with implications for metabolic disease and cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: A mosaic RBD-nanoparticle pan-sarbecovirus vaccine elicits nanobodies that target highly conserved epitopes
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, continually mutates, producing new variants of concern (VOCs). Substitutions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) have resulted in reduced efficacies of vaccines and therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. Indeed, since the emergence of Omicron and earlier VOCs, most previously approved anti-RBD therapeutic monoclonal antibodies are no longer authorized as therapeutics. To address VOC substitutions effects on therapeutic antibody efficacy, we sought to identify single-domain nanobodies (VHHs) targeting RBD regions (class 4, class 1/4, portions of class 3 and class 5 RBD epitopes) that are more conserved across VOCs, reasoning that the smaller size of camelid nanobodies compared with conventional two-domain antibody combining sites would facilitate access to occluded RBD epitopes. We used a Beacon optofluidic platform to isolate and characterize single memory B cells from a llama immunized with a mosaic RBD-nanoparticle immunogen that elicits broad antibody responses across sarbecoviruses. Using multiplex binding assays, we identified nanobodies that bind to spike RBDs from diverse sarbecovirus strains. Competition ELISAs and crystal structures of VHH-RBD complexes showed that isolated nanobodies recognize broadly conserved epitopes, including those on the RBD that are inaccessible to analogous conventional two-domain antibodies. Promising VHH-Fcs neutralized SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and zoonotic sarbecoviruses, demonstrating potential therapeutic utility for current and future outbreaks.

papers.title: Leishmania-infected human dendritic cells clear their intracellular parasites by a mechanism involving the cytolytic effector molecules granzyme B and granulysin
papers.abstract: Leishmania are intracellular parasites that cause various human diseases ranging from self-healing cutaneous to fatal visceral leishmaniasis. Host cells are phagocytes, primarily macrophages, where the parasites neutralize innate immune defenses, proliferate and finally rupture the cells. Despite that, Leishmania infection induces vigorous T cell responses, which require antigen processing and presentation, and stimulation by phagocytes, importantly dendritic cells. It was not clear how to align blockade of phagocyte functions with efficient immune stimulation. Here we show that, in contrast to macrophages, human dendritic cells survive the infection and destroy the parasites. This process involves granzyme B and granulysin, two cytolytic molecules essential for destruction of infected or otherwise aberrant cells by cytolytic T cells and natural killer cells. The report for the first time shows that these molecules not only act in target cell lysis by cytolytic effector cells but also in intracellular processing of infectious agents by dendritic cells.

papers.title: Dietary Exposure to Purified Gliadins and Avenins: Effects on Intestinal and Immune Responses in BALB/c Mice
papers.abstract: Dietary cereal prolamins differ in composition and gastrointestinal processing, but their shared and protein-source-specific effects on intestinal homeostasis remain incompletely defined. BALB/c mice were fed for five weeks with diets in which 70% of total protein was supplied by vital wheat gluten, purified gliadin, or purified avenin, alongside casein-fed controls. Intestinal morphology, antigen-specific plasma immunoglobulin G and A (IgG, IgA), mucosal gene expression, and small-intestinal proteomics were analysed. No overt histopathological injury or generalised inflammatory response was detected in any group. Gliadin and avenin both increased ileal villus length; avenin additionally elicited the broadest and most frequent prolamin-specific IgG response, associated with reduced intestinal interleukin-10 expression in responding animals. Proteomic profiling revealed a shared structural-metabolic signature alongside protein-specific changes in lipid handling, junctional regulation, and epithelial immune signalling. These findings indicate that wheat- and oat-derived prolamins differentially influence intestinal homeostasis and antigen recognition even at matched dietary doses, informing their evaluation as functional food ingredients.

papers.title: Structural Basis of γδ T-Cell Receptor Crosslinking and Activation by a Spontaneously Dimerized Fab
papers.abstract: The {gamma}{delta} T-cell receptor ({gamma}{delta} TCR) mediates immune responses in {gamma}{delta}T-cells, playing crucial roles in immune defense, tissue surveillance, and homeostasis. While recent studies suggest that {gamma}{delta} TCRs engage ligands multivalently (such as butyrophilins), the activation mechanism of the {gamma}{delta} TCR remains elusive. Here, we present the structures of the V{gamma}9V{delta}2 (clone G115) TCR in both the inactive and the Fab-crosslinked active states. The {gamma}{delta} TCR is a lipoprotein complex consisting of a TCR-{gamma}{delta} heterodimer surrounded by three CD3 dimers, CD3{delta}{epsilon}, CD3{gamma}{epsilon}, CD3{zeta}{zeta}. Lipids form a 'barrier' that isolates CD3{zeta} from the other {gamma}{delta} TCR subunits. Unexpectedly, we discover that the Fab fragment of the UCHT1 antibody dimerizes upon binding the V{gamma}9V{delta}2 TCR. This dimerized Fab acts as an agonist by crosslinking the receptor. Our cryo-EM structures of the Fab-crosslinked V{gamma}9V{delta}2 TCR reveal rigid 2:2 Fab:TCR tetramers in three conformations. Structural analysis identifies three Fab dimer interfaces, one between the light chains and two symmetrical ones between light chains and heavy chains. In addition to the expected Fab-CD3{epsilon} interface, glycan-Fab interactions likely contribute to the Fab:TCR tetramer assembly. We show that the dimerized V{gamma}9V{delta}2 TCR exhibits conformational plasticity. Furthermore, lipidomic mass spectrometry demonstrates that cholesterol and phosphatidylethanolamine are enriched within the inactive {gamma}{delta} TCR complex but are significantly depleted upon activation by the dimerized Fab. Our findings reveal a Fab-dimerization-driven activation mechanism, provide a basis for engineering rigid TCR-crosslinking agonists, and suggest that multivalency-induced clustering may represent a general paradigm for {gamma}V{delta} TCR activation.

papers.title: Early-life human lymphopoiesis generates a distinct B-cell lineage
papers.abstract: We characterize the first wave of human B-lymphopoiesis across gestation (n=42 donors) and identify a developmentally and functionally distinct B-cell lineage that shapes antibody specificity before birth. The earliest lymphoid progenitors engage an evolutionarily conserved genetic program enriched for imprinted genes associated with embryogenesis in mice and humans. These progenitors arise in the yolk sac and acquire Early B-cell Factor 1 (EBF1) in the embryonic liver, initiating B-lymphopoiesis before Hematopoietic Stem Cells emerge. Functionally, these early-life B-lymphoid progenitors (eBLPs; CD81hiTdT-IL3R+) respond to IL-3 to promote B-cell fate commitment and generate two waves of stereotyped public B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoires, shaping adaptive immunity at birth. The same molecular program and public BCRs are recapitulated during B-cell differentiation from pluripotent stem cells in vitro and after transplantation into humanized mice, where they generate antibody-secreting cells and SOX4+ B cells resembling infant lymphocytes. Developmental origin therefore intrinsically programs B-cell identity and antibody specificity.

papers.title: Noncanonical CD11b on CD8+ T cells promotes cytotoxic effector function
papers.abstract: Cancer immunosurveillance largely relies on effector CD8+ T cells, yet surface determinants of cytotoxic competence within tumor-reactive populations remain incompletely defined. Using single-cell surface proteomics in a mouse breast cancer model, we identified a tumor-enriched subset of antigen-experienced CD8+ T cells expressing CD11b, a prototypic myeloid integrin. CD11b CD8 T cells were detected across mouse tumor models and human solid tumors and, within tumor-reactive populations, CD11b marked cells with greater cytotoxic potential. Following activation, naive CD8+ T cells induced ITGAM transcription and CD18-dependent CD11b surface expression. Mechanistically, CD11b localized to the peripheral adhesive ring of the immune synapse and promoted lytic-granule secretion. Accordingly, CD11b+ T cells exhibited enhanced TCR- and CAR-mediated tumor cell killing, whereas CD11b deletion impaired T cell antitumor activity. Together, these findings identify CD11b as an inducible, noncanonical component of the T cell immune synapse that marks cytotoxic competence and promotes antitumor T cell function.

papers.title: Non-canonical IL-2 signaling facilitates peripheral regulatory T cell differentiation
papers.abstract: Non-canonical IL-2 signaling, termed Monoclonal antibody or Matrix-directed Alternative Cytokine Signaling (MACS), is mediated by a CD25-chemokine receptor complex and operates in concert with the canonical JAK-STAT5 pathway; however, its role in T cell homeostasis remains poorly defined. Here, we uncover a role for MACS in regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation and functional specification. We generated Il2E66K/E66K mice in which CD25-CCR7 assembly is disrupted and IL-2-induced STAT5 phosphorylation is preserved. Immunophenotyping analysis by flow cytometry revealed that MACS deficiency reduces the accumulation of Nrp1- Foxp3+ Tregs in gut-associated lymphoid tissues from 24-weeks-old Il2E66K/E66K mutant mice. Single-cell transcriptomics, functional suppression assays, and in vitro differentiation revealed that MACS engagement drives Treg differentiation and sustains effector Treg programs - marked by robust IL-10 expression - in part via an AP-1-dependent transcriptional network. These findings establish IL-2 MACS as a distinct signal directing peripheral immune tolerance and highlight a potential node for targeted immunomodulation.

papers.title: Hypothermic and Normothermic Machine Perfusion Differentially Shape the Renal Cellular Landscape
papers.abstract: The shortage of donor organs has led to an increased use of extended-criteria donors and donation after circulatory death for kidney transplantation, both of which are associated with graft injury. Although machine perfusion (MP) offers a preservation strategy, the most beneficial approach for kidneys with respect to effective graft preservation remains unclear. We compared oxygenated hypothermic (HMP) and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) using a murine kidney perfusion model regarding intra-graft immune cell composition, viability, and inflammatory responses. NMP resulted in more severe tubular injury, accompanied by increased immune cell mobilization out of the graft. NMP increased early apoptosis among kidney-resident immune-cell populations, whereas endothelial cells showed increased late apoptosis after both strategies. Proximal tubular-cell apoptosis remained comparable to naive tissue, and neither modality reduced reactive oxygen species levels. Both protocols induced antioxidant and hypoxia-responsive genes compared with static cold storage, while NMP elicited a stronger inflammatory response. Treatment with the senolytic ABT-263 demonstrated the models feasibility for investigating renal injury, cellular viability, and immune activation during MP.

papers.title: Keratinocyte FABP5 mediates saturated fat-induced MAPK/CCL20 signaling in psoriatic inflammation
papers.abstract: Saturated fats in high-fat diets (HFDs) have been associated with increased risk and severity of psoriasis. However, the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain to be further defined. Here, using a unique mouse strain with keratinocyte-specific deletion of fatty acid-binding protein 5 (FABP5) (Fabp5f/fKrt6a-Cre), we reported that keratinocyte FABP5 deletion significantly attenuated saturated HFD-exacerbated psoriatic symptoms. Immunological analyses demonstrated that FABP5 specific deletion in keratinocytes selectively reduced skin TCR {gamma} {delta} dim cell accumulation and IL-17A production. Further skin bulk-RNA and single-cell RNA sequence analyses showed a strong association of keratinocyte FABP5 with increased activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways under saturated HFD-induced obesity. Mechanistically, saturated fatty-acids (SFAs) induce FABP5-dependent MAPK activation and CCL20 production in keratinocytes, promoting the recruitment and activation of IL-17-producing {gamma}{delta} T cells in the skin. Together, these findings suggest a previously undefined FABP5/MAPK/CCL20 signaling axis that links saturated fats to exacerbated psoriatic inflammation.

papers.title: Maftivimab monotherapy is effective in a non-human primate model of Bundibugyo virus disease
papers.abstract: The 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has created an urgent need for treatments for BDBV disease, yet the only FDA-approved ebolavirus therapeutics, the monoclonal antibody (mAb) cocktail Inmazeb and the mAb Ebanga, are indicated for Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV). Maftivimab (REGN3479), the most potent neutralizing component of Inmazeb, targets ebolavirus species GPs broadly; however, how it engages BDBV GP, whether it neutralizes BDBV-2026, and whether it protects against BDBV disease in vivo are unknown. Here we show that Maftivimab binds to BDBV-2007 GP with high affinity and potently neutralizes pseudoviruses carrying GP from a 2007 reference strain and the 2026 outbreak lineage. Additionally, a cryo-electron microscopy structure of Maftivimab Fab bound to trimeric BDBV-2007 GP superimposes closely on the EBOV GP:Maftivimab complex; importantly, all GP contact residues are conserved between the 2007 and 2026 BDBV sequences. Finally, in cynomolgus macaques challenged with BDBV-2007, a single dose of Maftivimab monotherapy given 7 days after infection, after the onset of clinical disease, rescued 6 of 6 animals, whereas 5 of 6 placebo-treated animals succumbed. These findings demonstrate that Maftivimab neutralizes BDBV, binds to its epitope on BDBV GP and is efficacious in treating established BDBV disease in the macaque model. The data support its evaluation in clinical trials during the ongoing or future outbreak.

papers.title: APEX2 proximity labeling maps the mGBP2-proximal proteome at the Toxoplasma gondii parasitophorous vacuole
papers.abstract: Interferon-inducible guanylate binding proteins (GBPs) are large GTPases crucial for the host immune response against Toxoplasma gondii, a globally prevalent intracellular apicomplexan parasite. Upon infection, T. gondii forms a parasitophorous vacuole (PV) that protects the parasite from host intracellular defense mechanisms. Murine GBPs (mGBPs) can recognize these PVs and assemble into supramolecular homo- and heterocomplexes, which is an essential step for PV membrane disruption, ultimately enabling cell-autonomous immune control of vacuole-resident pathogens. Our previous work has shown that mGBP2 is an important factor in the immune control of T. gondii. To further elucidate the functions of mGBP2, we employed an APEX2-based proximity labeling strategy to biotinylate proteins in the vicinity of mGBP2 during T. gondii infection. Mass spectrometry analysis of the biotinylated proteins revealed several novel PV-associated proteins such as Cyclooxygenase 2 (COX2/ Ptgs2), Caspase 12 (Cas12), Annexin 11 (Anxa11), Calnexin (Canx), Galectin 3 (Gal3), and Transgelin (Tagln) and valosin-containing protein (VCP) that co-recruit with mGBP2 at T. gondii PVs. In addition, we investigated their regulation by IFN-{gamma} and determined that inhibition of COX2 severely impairs T. gondii growth, highlighting a critical role for COX2 for parasite survival.

papers.title: Prenatal immune priming to Plasmodium falciparum is characterized by multi-lineage T-cell responses that are influenced by maternal microchimerism and predict malaria outcomes
papers.abstract: In malaria endemic settings, the fetus may be exposed to Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) antigens leading to prenatal immune primming (PIP). The fetus also acquires a graft of maternal cells in utero, a phenomenon known as maternal microchimerism (MMc). We have previously identified that MMc at birth predicts altered malaria susceptibility in early childhood, and we hypothesized that this association may be mediated via two potential mechanisms. First, the fetus may acquire Pf-specific MMc T-cells that directly respond to postnatal parasitemia. Alternatively, MMc may indirectly influence the quantity or quality of PIP. To investigate this hypothesis, infant cord bloods from 97 Malian primigravidae were screened for MMc using qPCR. A subset of ten cord blood mononuclear cells with variable MMc levels were stimulated with purified Pf merozoite extract and activated T-cells were sorted by flow cytometry for scRNAseq analysis. Transcriptional profile was used to differentiate Pf-responsive versus bystander activated T-cells, and MMc cells were identified using the Cellector algorithm. Among Pf-responsive cells, we identified four key populations: activated CD4 T-cells, ZBTB16+ CD4 T-cells, activated V{delta}1+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells, and cytotoxic V{gamma}9V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells. The minority of sorted cells were of MMc origin; however, there was a strong association between the presence of MMc and the quantity and quality of PIP. MMc+ infants had significantly fewer Pf-responsive T-cells, as well as a shifted distribution of these cells with fewer ZBTB16+ CD4 and cytotoxic V{gamma}9V{delta}2+ {gamma}{delta} T-cells. Clinically, MMc was protective from incident parasitemia and febrile malaria, whereas the frequencies of ZBTB16+ CD4 and activated CD4 T-cells were associated with increased risk. Together, these data demonstrate that MMc influences malaria outcomes through regulation of offspring inflammatory responses to Pf.

papers.title: An ER Retrieval-and-Release System Reveals Ligand-Independent Basal Signaling by Cell Surface TCRs
papers.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) machinery comprises the ligand-binding TCR{beta} and the CD3 signaling dimers. Individual subunits are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and only the fully assembled TCRs reach the cell surface. We engineered a system to retained CD3{varepsilon} is in the ER. This allowed only partial TCR assembly, while continuous retrieval of CD3{varepsilon} from the Golgi back to the ER enabled complete assembly. Synchronous TCR release by biotin addition caused a transient increase in surface TCR abundance that gradually returned to steady-state levels. Mathematical modeling revealed that TCR levels were controlled by feedback mechanisms. Notably, surface-localized, but not ER-localized, TCRs spontaneously generated ligand-independent basal signaling. Phosphoproteomic analyses revealed that this signal is similar, but not identical, to ligand-induced TCR activation signals, with distinct phosphorylation patterns already evident at the CD3 subunits. Our findings establish the TCR retrieval-and-release system as a tool to investigate ligand-independent basal TCR signaling.

papers.title: The Human Contraceptive Antibody Targets A Semenogelin Galectin-3 N-Linked Glycan Complex on the Sperm Surface
papers.abstract: The human contraception antibody (HCA) is a non-hormonal topical contraceptive entering Phase II clinical trials that functions by agglutinating and immobilizing sperm. To date, the HCA epitope has been described as an N-linked polylactosamine glycan motif on CD52, but this assignment has been inferred only by colocalization with anti-CD52 and S19 antibodies in western blots. Here, we report that HCA may instead bind semenogelin-galectin-3 complexes associated with the sperm surface. Semenogelins are gel forming, highly glycosylated proteins, with molecular weights of 50-70 kDa that are cleaved into smaller segments that adhere to sperm during semen liquefaction. In this study, we isolated the HCA antigen from seminal plasma and sperm using an HCA affinity column and identified semenogelin by mass spectrometry. Western blot analysis of seminal plasma showed that HCA binds to a large smear of proteins with a higher apparent molecular mass than CD52, and that these may correspond to semenogelin sequences. Flow cytometric analysis of enzymatically deglycosylated sperm demonstrated that HCA binding requires sperm surface N-linked glycans. However, despite this apparent glycan dependence, HCA failed to bind any glycans represented on a comprehensive glycan microarray. In addition to semenogelin, Galectin-3 was identified in the HCA purified sperm lysates, supporting a model in which HCA recognizes semenogelin-derived glycopeptides that are tethered to the sperm surface via a galectin mediated interaction with an N-linked glycan. We found that O-linked glycan modifications on the semenogelin proteins contain LacNAc motifs that can bind to galectins. Finally, we found that depletion of galectins bound to the sperm surface by competitive inhibitors reduced HCA-mediated agglutination, and this could be rescued by addition of recombinant galectin-3/semenogelin-2 complexes to sperm cultures. Collectively, our findings suggest that HCA's binding site involves a semenogelin-galectin-3 complex anchored to the sperm surface via an N-linked glycan.

papers.title: Stemness overcomes IFNγ-induced antitumour exhaustion in human macrophages
papers.abstract: Macrophages hold great promise for antitumour therapies (1-4), particularly owing to their ability to infiltrate solid tumours (5). Yet therapeutic success has been limited (6,7), because macrophages exhibit rapid exhaustion of antitumorigenic activity in the tumour (5,8,9). Here, we induced a stem-like self-renewal programme in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived macrophages by deleting the self-renewal restricting transcription factors MAFB and MAF (MAF-DKO). Human MAF-DKO macrophages showed activated stem cell signatures, increased clonogenicity and proliferative potential. Increased self-renewal capacity was accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial fitness and invigorated energy metabolism. Importantly, these stemness features prevented exhaustion, cellular aging-associated parameters and loss of energy efficiency that are typically associated with proinflammatory macrophage activation. In addition, activated MAF-DKO macrophages showed a broad loss of IFN{gamma}-triggered immunosuppressive pathways (10,11), induced a super-activated state with robust cytotoxic activity and resisted exhaustion upon tumour cell exposure. Consequently, activated MAF-DKO macrophages showed intratumoral persistence with a stable antitumoral phenotype in vivo, conferred robust reduction of tumour burden and extended survival of tumour-bearing mice. Together, this demonstrates that the induction of stemness in human macrophages can overcome critical roadblocks of antitumour therapy by conferring resistance to activation-triggered exhaustion of antitumour activity in the TME.

papers.title: NOD2 restrains probiotic-mediated TLR2-dependent antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota influences cancer immunotherapy, but how interactions among host microbial sensors determine the activity of individual bacteria remains unclear. Here, we show that NOD2 restrains TLR2-dependent antitumor immunity induced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum. Oral administration of live or heat-killed L. plantarum enhanced immune checkpoint blockade efficacy in mouse tumor models. This activity required host TLR2 signaling and was diminished by disruption of bacterial lipoprotein. In contrast, NOD2 deficiency enhanced tumor control, intratumoral interferon-associated programs, and T cell activation. NOD2 deficiency also amplified chemokine and interferon-associated responses to L. plantarum and the synthetic TLR2 agonist Pam3CSK4 in myeloid cells. Genetic loss or pharmacological inhibition of NOD2 improved Pam3CSK4-mediated tumor control in combination with checkpoint blockade. These findings identify NOD2 as a functional checkpoint on TLR2-driven antitumor immunity and demonstrate that interactions between host microbial-sensing pathways shape the therapeutic activity of commensal bacteria and innate immune agonists.

papers.title: A 21-Color Spectral Flow Cytometry Panel for Comprehensive Immunophenotyping of Rat Tissues and a Companion 9-Color T-Cell Functional Assay
papers.abstract: Although rats are crucial translational research models due to their immunological homology and surgical feasibility, the scarcity of conjugated antibodies has hampered high-dimensional immune profiling. To bridge this gap, we created a synergistic two-panel method that uses full-spectral flow cytometry: a 21-color comprehensive immunophenotyping panel and a 9-color intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) panel. The 21-color panel navigates the limited fluorophore pool and maps innate and adaptive lineages at high resolution. While it can be used to profile neutrophils and monocytes in peripheral blood it reaches its full potential in lymphoid organs, allowing for the simultaneous evaluation of tissue-resident macrophages, dendritic cells, T cell differentiation (including Tregs), and APC function. Based on this phenotypic paradigm, the 9-color ICS panel dissects effector T cell activation and Th1/Th2/Th17 cytokine production. Furthermore, we reserved the PE color during panel creation, allowing for the use of antibodies and probes with PE or comparable fluorophores in conjunction with this panel, hence increasing overall flexibility. This combination technique, designed for rat peripheral blood, spleen, and lymph nodes, combines panoramic phenotyping with functional analysis, offering an adaptable foundation for complicated tissue microenvironments in tumor immunology, rheumatology, and autoimmunity research.

papers.title: Self-reactive human CD8⁺ T cells restricted by HLA-E mediate immunoregulatory and antiviral functions
papers.abstract: HLA-E constitutively presents self VL9 peptides on healthy cells, signaling an intact HLA class I pathway and protecting cells from natural killer cell attack. Beyond this canonical role, HLA-E-restricted CD8 T cells that recognize foreign pathogen peptides have emerged as mediators of immunity in multiple human infections, with orthologous responses conferring unprecedented protection in an HIV vaccine model. However, the poor stability of most pathogen-derived HLA-E ligands raises the possibility that additional modes of HLA-E-restricted recognition remain undiscovered. Here, we establish an alternative paradigm in which HLA-E-restricted CD8+ T cells recognize disease-associated increases in self-VL9/HLA-E rather than foreign antigen. These cells, which we term E-sensors, integrate activating and inhibitory signals to discriminate physiological from pathological levels of HLA-E expression. We demonstrate that E-sensors selectively eliminate highly activated, proliferating immune cells that express high levels of HLA-E, establishing a mechanistically resolved pathway of human CD8+ T cell immunoregulation. E-sensors also recognize pathogen-induced HLA-E upregulation and directly eliminate infected cells without prior pathogen-specific priming, demonstrating immediate immunosurveillance through recognition of increased self. Consistent with this antiviral function, we establish E-sensors as a previously unrecognized component of spontaneous HIV immune control in persons who naturally control infection. Together, our findings establish a pathway of human immunosurveillance and immunoregulation in which CD8 T cells detect pathological increases in a constitutively expressed non-classical HLA class I molecule presenting a conserved self-peptide. This disease-agnostic mechanism of immune recognition has implications across infection, cancer, autoimmune disease, and other pathologies that upregulate HLA-E. Unlike classical HLA class I molecules, the near-monomorphic nature of HLA-E further positions this pathway as an untapped effector axis, warranting investigation as a potential target for immune interventions.

papers.title: Dual-Antigen CCHFV Vaccine Induces Neutralizing Immunity and Protection Against Lethal Challenge
papers.abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is a WHO-priority pathogen with high mortality and wide global distribution. A major challenge in CCHFV vaccine development is identifying antigens that induce functional cellular and humoral immunity. We previously showed that the CCHF nucleoprotein (NP) elicits protective responses in mice and non-human primates but does not induce neutralizing antibodies. We therefore systematically screened six chimeric DNA vaccines expressing different CCHF glycoproteins combined with NP. A construct comprising the ectodomain of the glycoprotein Gc and NP elicited robust antibody and T-cell responses to both antigens. The Gc-NP gene was subsequently developed as a lipid nanoparticle-formulated mRNA vaccine using a scalable manufacturing pipeline. Gc-NP mRNA-LNP induced robust antigen-specific humoral and cellular responses comparable to those elicited by the corresponding DNA vaccine, despite the substantially lower dose. Both vaccine approaches generated Gc-directed neutralizing antibody responses against CCHFV pseudovirus and protected mice against homologous Hoti and heterologous IbAr10200 strain challenge. These findings demonstrate that systematic antigen screening combined with genetic vaccine platforms can identify a potent multi-antigen CCHF vaccine candidate.

papers.title: Human caspase-4 and caspase-5 assemble into non-canonical inflammasomes in response to overlapping and distinct LPS structures
papers.abstract: Innate immune sensing of bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is critical to host defense, but a dysregulated response can lead to sepsis, a life-threatening condition associated with multiple organ failure and shock. LPS is sensed at the cell surface by Toll-Like Receptor 4 (TLR4) and in the cytosol by mouse caspase-11 (Casp11) or its human orthologs, caspase-4 and 5 (CASP4/5). In response to cytosolic LPS, Casp11 oligomerizes in a catalytically dependent manner into supramolecular organizing centers (SMOCs). We demonstrate that CASP4 and CASP5 also form catalytically dependent SMOCs in response to bacterial LPS in macrophages. Furthermore, we find that CASP4 and CASP5 differentially respond to distinct LPS structural variants that fail to activate CASP11 and that only activating LPS structures induce SMOC formation by the corresponding caspase. Notably, transgenic mice expressing CASP4 in lieu of Casp11 exert more effective control of Francisella novicida, a rodent pathogen whose LPS evades TLR4 and Casp11 detection. Conversely, CASP4-expressing mice are more susceptible to sepsis when exposed to E. coli expressing a lipid A variant that fails to activate TLR4 and Casp11. Together, these findings reveal human CASP4 and CASP5 have evolved to assemble into SMOCs in response to a broader range of LPS structures than mouse Casp11 and highlight the potential tradeoff between systemic inflammation and control of bacterial infection that may underline these differences. Our findings may inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for gram-negative bacterial infection and sepsis that are effective in humans.

papers.title: In vitro-generated murine monocyte-derived dendritic cells habor a unique identity compared to other mononuclear phagocytes, largely conserved with their human and putative in vivo counterparts.
papers.abstract: Whether the cells differentiating in vitro from total murine bone marrow (BM) cultures with GM-CSF +/- IL-4 are homologous to the human cells derived in vitro from purified circulating monocytes (Mo) cultured with GM-CSF and IL-4, mostly correspond to monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) or rather to macrophages (MFs), and have in vivo counterparts, is debated. It has been proposed to define cell types based on their ontogeny, leading to the proposal of excluding from the dendritic cell (DC) family the cells that do not arise from the common DC progenitors (CDP). However, recent discoveries support defining cell types rather by functions, or, as a surrogate, their instructive molecular networks. Indeed, Langerhans cells, Rorgt+ DCs, some cDC2As and human in vitro-derived moDCs do not arise from the CDP but exert hallmark DC functions instructed by specific transcriptomic modules shared with cDCs. Actually, the study of both LCs and moDCs has been key for dissecting DC biology. Yet, the existence of moDCs is put into questions. The functions once attributed to moDCs are now proposed to be exerted by type 2B conventional DCs (cDC2Bs) or type 3 DCs (DC3s) that have been characterized recently, harbor strongly overlapping phenotypes with moDCs and a similar mixed expression of genes from both the cDC and Mo/MF lineages, but a different ontogeny. To clarify these issues, we generated a transcriptomic atlas of in vitro-derived mononuclear phagocytes (MNPs). We show that moDCs are the only DC type arising in BM cultures in the presence of GM-CSF and IL-4. They express a unique transcriptomic and phenotypic signature, different from those of cDC2Bs and DC3s that are produced in FLT3-L cultures and appear to correspond to the same DC type differentiating though two different but converging ontogenetic paths. By harnessing the phenotypic and transcriptomic signatures identified from the analysis of our in vitro MNP atlas, we are able to identify in vivo a population of putative DCs differentiated from monocytes derived from the common monocyte-granulocyte progenitor (GMP), in a respiratory allergy model, specifically in the lungs of mice sensitized to house dust mite (HDM). Using the model of thioglycolate-induced peritonitis, we also characterized the CD226+ Mo-derived cells that have been reported to be moDCs or small cavity MFs (SCM) depending on studies. We showed that these cells are mainly differentiated from monocytes derived from the MDP, and split into two populations, one resembling MFs (SCMs) and the other one closer to lung moDCs but expressing distinct genes suggesting a different functional potential. Collectively, we show that the generation and characterization of specific MNP types in vitro can be harnessed to rigorously define their in vivo counterparts based on phenotypic analysis and gene module assessment, as we demonstrate for moDCs.

papers.title: Fever-range temperature enhances B cells in vitro but is dispensable for the germinal center in vivo
papers.abstract: Fever is a conserved physiological response to immune activation characterized by elevated body temperature. While hyperthermia enhances innate and T cell immunity, its role in shaping the B cell compartment remains poorly defined, despite B cells' role in long-term protection. Understanding how temperature modulates B cell physiology is relevant to vaccine strategies, particularly fever management around immunization. Therefore, we investigated the influence of fever-range thermal changes on humoral immunity. To decipher the direct effects, primary B cells from C57BL/6 mice were stimulated in vitro under mild hyperthermic conditions (~1.5{degrees}C increase). Fever-range temperature enhanced B cell activation, facilitated entry into cell division, and increased antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells, while transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of pathways involved in protein synthesis and mitochondrial respiration. To determine whether these intrinsic effects translated into altered humoral immunity in vivo, we developed a novel tunable implant-based system to induce localized, 48-hour hyperthermia around a draining lymph node in awake mice without altering core body temperature. Following subcutaneous NP-OVA/alum immunization, localized hyperthermia localized hyperthermia did not enhance antigen-specific germinal center B cell expansion, antibody titers or IgG affinity on day 9. Moreover, heating during priming did not affect the recall humoral response after a booster on day 21. Thus, fever-range temperature directly modulates murine B cell function in vitro but does not enhance humoral immunity in vivo, indicating that the biological consequences of intrinsic B cell thermosensitivity depend on its integration within the multicellular and inflammatory signals shaping germinal center responses.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory macrophages limit endothelial inflammation and restrict neutrophil recruitment through Gas6/AXL signaling
papers.abstract: Neutrophil extravasation requires coordinated interactions between the endothelium and surrounding cells, including tissue resident macrophages. Macrophages adopt distinct polarization states in the tissue environment, positioning them as regulators of vascular inflammation. However, how these states influence barrier function and neutrophil extravasation remains unclear. Here, we polarized macrophages in the matrix surrounding an endothelial vessel, in a three-dimensional inflammation-on-a-chip model developed only from primary human cells. We found anti-inflammatory macrophages limited endothelial inflammation, reducing ICAM-1 upregulation, maintaining VE-Cadherin expression, halving permeability relative to pro-inflammatory devices, and reducing neutrophil extravasation and migration relative to macrophage-free devices. Secretome profiling identified Gas6, an AXL ligand, as a potential regulator of these effects. Inhibiting AXL increased extravasation in devices with anti-inflammatory macrophages, and soluble Gas6 reduced extravasation in macrophage-free devices, implicating Gas6 as a mediator of this regulation. This indicates macrophages regulate endothelial inflammation and the neutrophil response via Gas6 signaling.

papers.title: Apoptotic Cells Promote Tim4+ Macrophage Differentiation Through Direct and Indirect Signaling Pathways
papers.abstract: Tissue macrophages are the primary cells responsible for efficiently clearing apoptotic cells, yet how professional efferocyte populations are established remains unclear. Tim4 marks a subset of macrophages across multiple tissues that are highly efferocytic, but the mechanisms governing Tim4 acquisition are poorly understood. Here, we show that monocyte-derived macrophages progressively differentiate into Tim4 macrophages in homeostatic and pathological settings. We identify a cell-autonomous pathway in which efficient apoptotic cell clearance promotes Tim4 acquisition in macrophages, as combined deficiency of CD11b and MerTK impairs both efferocytosis and Tim4 acquisition. Surprisingly, excessive apoptotic cell burden enhanced Tim4 acquisition independently of these receptors. We demonstrate that serial exposure to apoptotic cells induces a type 2 immune response characterized by expansion of IL-4-producing populations and that IL-4R-STAT6 signaling is sufficient and required to drive Tim4 acquisition. These findings support a model in which Tim4 acquisition in macrophages integrates direct signals associated with apoptotic cell clearance and indirect signals generated by apoptotic cell burden. We propose that these complementary mechanisms enable tissues to dynamically adjust the size and function of the professional efferocyte compartment to meet changing demands for apoptotic cell clearance.

papers.title: Diacylglycerol Kinases Balance DAG Signaling to Control B Cell Maturation, Germinal Center Homeostasis, and Humoral Immunity
papers.abstract: Diacylglycerol (DAG) is a critical second messenger downstream of the B-cell receptor (BCR), but how DAG signaling is regulated during B-cell development and humoral responses remains incompletely understood. Here, complementary gain- and loss-of-function approaches revealed stage-specific requirements for diacylglycerol kinase (DGK)-regulated signaling in B cells. Expression of the gain-of-function DGK{zeta} mutant DGK{zeta}{Delta}NLS had limited effects on early BM B-cell development but progressively impaired transitional and mature B-cell populations. DGK{zeta}{Delta}NLS attenuated BCR-induced ERK1/2 and mTOR signaling, activation, and proliferation and, when expressed in AID-expressing B cells, reduced GC B-cell survival and T-dependent IgG responses without detectably impairing GC B-cell proliferation in vivo. Conversely, combined DGK/{zeta} deficiency resulted in marked spontaneous GC B-cell expansion associated with enhanced ERK1/2, Akt, and S6 signaling and increased glucose uptake. Despite this steady-state GC expansion, DGK/{zeta}-deficient mice developed spontaneous autoreactivity and mounted impaired antigen-specific antibody responses. Thus, B-cell developmental stages exhibit differential sensitivity to altered DGK activity, and opposing perturbations of DGK-regulated signaling produce reciprocal effects on GC B-cell accumulation while both compromise productive humoral immunity. These findings identify DGKs as critical regulators that tune lipid signaling for B-cell maturation, GC homeostasis, and effective antibody responses.

papers.title: TLR7-Dependent Autoimmunity Remodels Intestinal Immune Cell Dissemination
papers.abstract: Intestinal immune cell dissemination has emerged as a fundamental mechanism of tissue-to-tissue immune communication that shapes systemic immunity, yet how this physiological process changes across different stages of systemic autoimmunity remains poorly understood. Here, using photoconversion, inducible and spontaneous models of TLR7-dependent autoimmunity, and microbiota perturbation, we define how autoimmunity reshapes intestinal immune dissemination. TLR7-dependent autoimmunity progressively suppresses dissemination in a tissue-dependent manner across gut-associated and systemic tissues while selectively reconfiguring the intestinal emigrant pool, characterized by reduced lymphocyte dissemination and increased representation of myeloid populations, particularly dendritic cells. This divergence is already evident in young TLR7-transgenic mice before detectable splenomegaly. Moreover, microbial regulation of intestinal dissemination depends on timing and inflammatory context, with antibiotic treatment during ongoing autoimmunity producing broader changes in intestinal immune dissemination. Together, our findings establish remodeling of physiological intestinal immune dissemination as an early feature of TLR7-dependent autoimmunity and reveal how chronic inflammation reshapes tissue-to-tissue immune communication.
